subject: MAP: Medivault capacity reservation — acceptance criteria & staggered GPU sizing
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@medivault.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft — capacity reservation & acceptance criteria

Alyssa — attaching a first-draft Mutual Action Plan tailored to the capacity reservation and acceptance window we discussed. Key asks below and a proposed staggered sizing approach to account for your production ramp.

Attachments: Medivault_MAP_v1.pdf, gpu-sizing_medivault.xlsx

Summary (high level)
- Target close: 2027-03-25 (final signature)
- Initial staging tranche: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (30-day ramp)
- Production bucket: 32 x A100-equivalent (on 60-day lead time after signature)
- Acceptance criteria: throughput smoke test + a set of 5 canonical prompts (see sheet) and SOC2 access checklist

Specific asks for your team
1) Confirm the 30/60-day split works for your internal timeline.
2) Approve the acceptance test prompt set (gpu-sizing_medivault.xlsx tab 'Evals').
3) Procurement: confirm PO format and expected billing start date.

If we can lock signoff on the MAP and PO by Thu (03/25), we can prioritize your tranches in our next GPU procurement batch and honor the quoted lead times. If you prefer a larger initial tranche, we can recalculate the ramp but it will shift the delivery windows by ~2–3 weeks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call anytime this week to walk through.

—
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — capacity reservation & acceptance criteria

Evelyn — thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachment:

- Lead times: our infra team is asking if the 60-day production bucket can be pushed earlier to 45 days if we commit to a 12-month reserved term. Is that an option?
- Acceptance tests: the canonical prompts look good but we need an additional throughput test that simulates mixed-length chat traffic; can your eval team add a short script example?
- PO: Procurement needs the vendor legal name and W-9 to include with the PO; I can share once I have the W-9.

We prefer an initial staging tranche of 12 GPUs (instead of 8) to validate latency percentiles under load. If that increases the initial delivery window, flag the change and we will weigh trade-offs.

Alyssa
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Medivault

Eve — quick internal readout after Alyssa's ask:

- 45-day production lead time is feasible if Medivault commits to a 12-month reserved term and a minimal guaranteed utilization (we should propose 60% baseline to make the accelerated procurement case). Finance will need that commitment in writing.
- Initial tranche: moving from 8 -> 12 GPUs increases scheduling pressure by one procurement slot; realistically adds ~10 business days to the staging tranche unless we shift a burst buffer from another tranche.
- Acceptance tests: solutions team can add a mixed-length chat throughput script; I'll attach a template snippet to the MAP before we send.

Recommendation: propose two options in the MAP for signoff — Option A (accelerated) = 12 initial GPUs + 45-day production lead time with 12-month term; Option B (standard) = 8 initial GPUs + 60-day lead time. Present both to the customer so procurement has a clear decision path.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa — thanks, that feedback is helpful. I updated the MAP to include the two-option path Karthik suggested and added a short mixed-traffic throughput script in the 'Evals' tab. See attached updated MAP and sizing sheet.

High-level changes (see attached Medivault_MAP_v1.pdf):
- Option A (accelerated): 12 initial GPUs -> production 32 GPUs on 45-day lead time; requires 12-month reserved term + 60% guaranteed utilization. Estimated billing start = date-of-signature.
- Option B (standard): 8 initial GPUs -> production 32 GPUs on 60-day lead time; standard 6-month reserved term available.
- Acceptance window: final signoff test to be run within 14 days of final tranche availability.

Next steps for Medivault
1) Procurement: share W-9 + PO template (we'll slot your PO into DocuSign once we have it).
2) Technical: confirm the eval prompt set + agree on the throughput script schedule (we recommend running tests during your low-traffic window).
3) Commercial: confirm which option (A or B) and sign; we will then issue a DocuSign with tranche dates locked.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.com/sign/MDV-487
Attached: Medivault_MAP_v1.pdf, gpu-sizing_medivault.xlsx

If this looks good I can circulate the DocuSign by EOD and route to Procurement and Ops for signatures. Would you prefer a short call to finalize?

Best,
